correctness.rationale: The partition of factors by 0–4 runs yields a closed formula without repeated factors. A four-run factor is a pair of palindromes exactly when its initial zero run equals the full second zero run, or its final one run equals the full preceding one run. Four parameter regions, reduced to three by complement-reversal symmetry, give algebraic strict bounds for n>=10. Exhaustive direct enumeration of all 126 four-run compositions at n=4..9 closes the finite boundary. A separate direct substring/split checker matches the formula for all 715 four-run compositions n=4..13, and checks explicit three-run witnesses. No finite experiment is asserted as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Borchert–Rampersad 2015 (Section 4) states the global extremal value as a conjecture and provides the three-run lemma, not the exact four-run distinct-factor formula or an all-length exclusion. Guo–Shallit–Shur 2015 concerns characterization/enumeration of palindrome pairs themselves; its statements do not imply the present uniform distinct-factor bound without new counting and optimization. Focused published-record and literature searches found no directly covering result; unindexed work remains a risk.

value.rationale: The result excludes an entire natural infinite class—four-run words—from the proposed extremal candidates of a published unsolved palindrome-pair factor problem. The four-run class is the first beyond the obvious three-run witnesses; a new formula together with length-uniform inequalities explains exactly why it is deficient. This is a structural partial result, not an arbitrary finite case or routine restatement of the three-run lemma.
